title: Registration fee for guaranteed job vs. fee-free interview scheduling
summary: A recruiter from TalentBridge Staffing calls about the recipient's profile on NaukriHub for a customer-support role at Vistara Infotech. In the fraud case, the recruiter promises a guaranteed offer and asks for a "registration fee" to a personal UPI ID before any interview. In the legitimate case, the recruiter schedules an interview and states that candidates never pay anything.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a job seeker with a recent profile on NaukriHub; education and experience sampled at generation.
other_facts: Role: customer-support executive, salary [AMOUNT_2] (₹18,000–₹35,000 per month), location [CITY].
Both callers mention the recipient's portal profile and the role.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller demands payment from a candidate before any selection process, to a personal account, in exchange for a guaranteed job.
fraud.caller_objective: Collect the registration fee; there is no job.
stable_facts: Payment to [UPI_ID_1], a personal-looking handle, not a company account.
The caller says the offer letter is "guaranteed" and will be sent after payment.
The caller claims "limited seats" closing today.

The caller asks the recipient to reply to an email from the agency's official address with an updated resume.
The employer pays the agency; candidates pay nothing.

cooperative.fraud: Agrees to pay and asks for the UPI ID again

clarifying.fraud: Asks why a fee is needed and whether it is refundable
clarifying.legitimate: Asks what the interview will cover and about shift timings

resistant.fraud: Says they will not pay before an interview
resistant.legitimate: Says the slot does not suit them and asks for another

suspicious.fraud: Says genuine companies do not charge candidates and asks if this is fraud
suspicious.legitimate: Asks how they can verify the agency is genuine

fraud: caller offers a "discount" and recipient declines
legitimate: caller suggests checking the agency's official website and email.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may lower the fee, add urgency, or claim the fee is refundable. They must not switch to asking for bank credentials. The legitimate caller must not mention any payment after the branch.

must_preserve: role and salary identical across _F and _L
fee request to personal UPI at turn 7 in _F
must_not_emit: the words "scam" or "fraud" in caller lines

ambiguities: Both calls are unsolicited and both reference the job portal profile. Unsolicited contact is not evidence.
Refundable" fees are still fraud_attempt in this family. Legitimate paid services (for example resume writing sold openly) belong in jr_15, not here.
Salary above market is not used as evidence; it is held identical across cases.

evidence_references.claim: Upfront payment is a red flag in fake job schemes (C11)
Fraud can be reported on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in (C12)
